subject.title: fix(models): add provider request rate limits

question: Should OpenClaw accept `models.providers.*.request.rateLimit` as a core provider-dispatch config surface now, or keep rate limiting blocked behind the broader outbound-governance design?
rationale: The PR is a focused implementation, but it creates public config and runtime failure semantics while the canonical issue still needs maintainer scoping for budgets, CLI/status, tool/channel calls, and backoff behavior.

options.title: Accept Provider-Dispatch Slice After Rebase
options.body: Land this opt-in provider HTTP pacing surface after conflict resolution preserves current egress security behavior, and track budgets/status/backoff/tools separately.

options.title: Require Broader Rate-Limit Design First
options.body: Pause this PR until maintainers define one outbound-governance API across provider dispatch, tools, budgets, status, and CLI UX.

options.title: Defer Core Config Surface
options.body: Close or hold this PR and keep rate limiting as a plugin/API-seam discussion until core ownership is clearer.

recommendation.title: Accept Provider-Dispatch Slice After Rebase
recommendation.body: Land this opt-in provider HTTP pacing surface after conflict resolution preserves current egress security behavior, and track budgets/status/backoff/tools separately.

likelyOwner.reason: They own the strongest recent provider egress/security history and are the best available product-scope owner from the likely owner set.
